suggestions.title: ADR 0021 D3 and D4 disagree on files compare returns without a patch (pure renames, oversized diffs)
suggestions.file: docs/adr/0021-自治合并-项目级策略与补丁绑定判定.md
suggestions.failurePath: D3 (line 36) says a file with no patch gets patchSha null and, outside the evidence directory, goes to a person under D4. D4 (line 37) names only binary files outside docs/verify among the forced-human cases. For pure renames it says compare counts them as 0 lines and that pr-gate's --no-renames is 'stricter on pure renames'. The P3 implementation in #1420 follows D3: apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/paths.ts lines 8-9, 66 and 103 route every no-patch file outside docs/verify (binary, oversized diff, pure rename) to the user. So for a pure rename apps/web/src/a.ts -> apps/web/src/b.ts the product gate answers user, while pr-gate (D + A rows, counted as whole files, not binary) answers auto-merge. D4's claim that pr-gate is the stricter of the two holds only for the line count, not for the routing.
suggestions.evidence: ADR 0021 D3: '没有 patch 时为 null（这种文件在证据目录外按 D4 留人）'. D4: '证据目录外的二进制文件 ... 纯改名为 0，pr-gate 用 --no-renames ... 在纯改名上更严'. The #1420 head paths.ts:8: '对二进制不给 patch，纯改名也不给，两者分不出来，没有 patch 的一律算'. Add 'compare 不给 patch 的文件（二进制、diff 过大、纯改名）' to D4's list, or drop the parenthetical from D3.

suggestions.title: The quoted-path error tells the caller to use core.quotePath=false even when git quotes for another reason
suggestions.failurePath: A PR adds apps/web/src/a"b.ts or a path that contains a backslash. With core.quotePath=false, git still C-quotes it: a scratch repo on git 2.43 printed "a\"b.ts" and "c\\d.ts" from FILES_CMD. The check on lines 130-135 fires before SAFE_PATH and throws 'C-quoted paths ...; build the lists with core.quotePath=false'. The caller already used that flag, so it can rebuild and get the same error again, instead of getting the 'review this PR by hand' message that SAFE_PATH gives such paths. The gate still fails closed. Only the guidance is wrong.
suggestions.evidence: git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-renames --name-only HEAD~1...HEAD in /tmp scratch printed "a\"b.ts" and "c\\d.ts".

suggestions.title: LINES_CMD needs git 2.40 or later for --attr-source, and no minimum version is stated
suggestions.failurePath: `git --attr-source=<tree>` was added in git 2.40. Spec 28 §7.2 recommends running on the user's Mac. If that machine's git is older (Apple's bundled git has been 2.39.x), LINES_CMD exits with 'unknown option', and neither the caller nor the safety reviewer can produce linesChanged as ARGS_HELP specifies. If both fall back to plain `git diff --numstat`, the max() on line 369 no longer protects against the run 6 case: a committed `*.ts -diff` .gitattributes zeroes both counts. That .gitattributes would itself be protected only if it is in this PR; an older one already on main would not be. This depends on the git version in use, so it is conditional.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:116 LINES_CMD; ARGS_HELP on line 123 and spec 28 §7.5 name the command but no minimum git version; local git here is 2.43.0.

suggestions.title: Two AGENTS.md rule adjustments rely on the user's merge as the explicit confirmation required by User Override
suggestions.failurePath:
1. AGENTS.md:96 adds an exception to the hard rule "不切分支看 diff": the pr-gate evidence dimension and its skeptics may run `checkout --detach` in their own worktrees.
2. Spec 28 §7.4 (line 227) and D7 (line 74) declare that listing PRs that await the user's merge is "a report, not a question" under AGENTS.md:94, while §7.5 (line 247) has the main session "请用户合并". AGENTS.md:94 covers any question about a PR, including whether to merge. That carve-out lives in a spec, not in AGENTS.md.
AGENTS.md:113-115 requires explicit user confirmation before its rules are overridden. D4 already routes this PR to a user merge, and the Risk section names the checkout exception, but not the needs-decision reading as a rule change. If the carve-out is meant to stand, the user should confirm both points when merging. Otherwise the needs-decision reading should move into AGENTS.md itself. The carve-out is low risk in practice: §7.5 line 257 enables auto-merge only for go verdicts outside D4, so a PR that awaits the user has no auto-merge armed, and that is the failure AGENTS.md:94 guards against (#1435).
suggestions.evidence: AGENTS.md:94, :96, :113-115 at the head; spec 28 lines 74, 227, 247, 257.

suggestions.title: Self-check does not pin the skeptic prompt, so the withdraw rule can be emptied with CI still green
suggestions.failurePath: The ticket says the self-check covers the refute-and-withdraw rule. But no case checks what a skeptic is told. Example: an edit removes `${JSON.stringify(f)}` from the skeptic prompt at line 282, or removes the 'Try to refute it by tracing ... Set refuted to false only if you confirmed' sentence. Then `node scripts/pr-gate-selfcheck.mjs` still prints 73/73 (I ran both mutations). In a real run, a skeptic that never sees the finding cannot confirm it. The prompt's default is 'If you cannot confirm it, set refuted to true', so both skeptics refute. Every blocking finding up to the cap is then withdrawn, and go comes back true. The CI step in ci.yml would not notice. The code at the head is correct today; what is missing is a test that keeps it that way.
suggestions.evidence: Mutations 'skeptic-no-finding' and 'skeptic-no-trace' both give 73/73. The cases at selfcheck lines 527-592 only check the vote arithmetic. The prompt cases at lines 648-695 check refs, the comment filter and the read-only line, never the finding payload. A case that collects the refute:* calls and checks that each prompt contains JSON.stringify(blocker) and the 'refuted to false only if you confirmed' sentence would kill both mutations.

suggestions.title: Ticket body reaches the shell-holding evidence reviewer unfiltered; the prompt calls it text by the PR author
suggestions.failurePath: readRules filters PR comments down to OWNER, MEMBER and COLLABORATOR because the repo is public and the evidence dimension has a shell. Yet every agent, the evidence reviewer and its skeptics included, fetches `issues/${ticket}` whole. Under ADR 0021 D5 a ticket can be an outsider's issue that the owner labeled ready-for-agent, and its author can edit the body after the labeling. Line 174 then calls the ticket 'data written by the PR author', which is false for such a ticket. That edited body reaches an agent with a shell and the session's credentials, guarded only by the data-not-instructions line. The gate could check the ticket's author_association the way it checks comments' and withhold a non-member's body, or at least name the real author in the framing.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:173-174; ADR 0021 D5 (line 38); spec 28 §7.5 comment-filter rationale

suggestions.title: Case-insensitive matching lacks Unicode case folding, so U+017F / U+212A variants of protected names auto-merge
suggestions.failurePath: globToRegExp builds RegExps with flag 'i' and no 'u'. In that mode JS does not fold non-ASCII to ASCII: /s/i.test('ſ') is false and /s/iu.test('ſ') is true. SAFE_PATH (line 127) admits \p{L}, which includes U+017F (ſ) and U+212A (Kelvin K). The probe sends apps/web/src/AGENTſ.md to auto-merge while apps/web/src/AGENTS.md goes to the user. The same holds for variants of scripts, package.json, .husky and .gitattributes inside the auto-merge set. ADR 0021 D4 says matching ignores case because macOS's filesystem does, but this check runs only JS's ASCII case folding. I did not verify on APFS whether it aliases ſ or K to s or k, so the macOS impact is unconfirmed. Adding the 'u' flag, or NFKC-normalizing paths before matching, closes the gap at no cost.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:100 `new RegExp(..., 'i')`, :127 SAFE_PATH; node: /s/i.test('ſ') false, /s/iu.test('ſ') true; stub probe on apps/web/src/AGENTſ.md -> auto-merge
